text: To make the case for something
I am applying in order to close a gap I can already see.
I chose an online format so that I could keep running the company.
The residencies are short, so most participants keep working.
The company grew faster than I did, which is why I am applying now.
I was on the fence for two years, and then I saw the ceiling.
How international is the cohort this year?

The answer we hear too often is that the candidate wants to grow and broaden their horizons, and I want to be fair about this: it is almost always sincere. The trouble is that it is true of every single person who applies, so it makes the case for nobody in particular. When we ask why now, we are not asking a polite version of why. We are asking what changed. Something moved in the last year or two, and if you cannot name it, the committee will assume that nothing did, and that you are applying because it seemed like the right stage of life. And let me say something about the people who have been thinking about this for years. Being on the fence is not a problem. Half the strongest candidates I have interviewed were on the fence for a long time. What matters is whether they can tell me what pushed them off it. The ones who cannot are usually the ones we do not shortlist.

The page says ten to fifteen hours a week, and that number is honest. What nobody tells you is which hours they are. They come out of the evening, and they come out of Sunday, and your family will notice before you do. I would still do it again, but I would have that conversation at home first instead of in month four. The residency weeks surprised me. I assumed they were the teaching, and they are not, because honestly you could do that part online. The residencies are where the cohort turns into a group of people you would actually call, and that is the part that is still there two years after the program ended. My one piece of advice is about the capstone. Choose the problem you are already avoiding at work. You are going to spend a year on it either way, so it may as well be the one that is costing you money.
